digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler retry and outcome contract
propositions: Nested subprocess/SDK/wrapper retries cause timeout-amplified or ambiguous Jira writes; a single provider-neutral retry budget with stable logical id and desired postcondition contract is required to guarantee at most three invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep per operation.

Jira has no idempotency key, so recovery must observe desired state before replay and distinguish satisfied observation (recovered success), conclusive old state (remaining-budget replay permitted), and failed/inconclusive observation (non-replaying commit_unknown).

Cloud and DC summary-write executors must be internally selected (defaulting to legacy in S1, no config/env surface), with exact {"summary"}-only routes bypassing generic retry and mixed fields remaining one legacy call.

DC summary invocation is exactly GET→PUT→GET with no hidden repeats; failure ends that invocation; successful read-back is authoritative; Cloud makes one ACLI process per write with sanitized exit/stdout/stderr decoding and recovery via primary-store REST get_issue_by_rest with one-attempt/no-sleep policy.

Every terminal/exhausted outcome must emit exactly one redacted completion log containing only logical id, disposition, invocation count, request count, cleanup status, retry_not_before, and one message (≤512 code points), with the whole log ≤1,024 code points.

Jira 3.10.5 dedicated executor client must pass max_retries=0 and fail fast if _session.max_retries≠0; an offline construction test against the real jira library must validate this seam before executor logic layers on it, mirroring the guard pattern at llm/anthropic_model.py.
